summary: Regression testing of PATCH /expenses and /deliveries after exclude_none=True -> exclude_unset=True fix. All 4 focused tests passed (100%). Bug from iteration_4 is fully resolved: partial PATCH with only {status:'approved'} now preserves amount/value/quantity/customer/driver. Activity log correctly records expense_approved.
critical_code_review_comments: ResourceInput is used as a single mega-schema for products/deliveries/expenses/customers - consider splitting for clearer validation, though exclude_unset=True mitigates the immediate risk.
update_delivery lacks admin_user guard (uses current_user) - any authenticated driver can mutate any delivery. Verify if intended.
PATCH /expenses always overwrites reviewed_by/reviewed_at even when payload is a non-status field update - acceptable for now but couples audit fields to any admin edit.
seed_data_creation: Created TEST_ prefixed expenses and deliveries via API; not cleaned up (small volume, non-blocking).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression suite for PATCH partial updates lives at /app/backend/tests/test_patch_preserve_fields.py. Prior iteration_4 bug is fixed. update_delivery uses current_user (not admin_user) - flagged for review, not tested against as it may be intentional (drivers marking own deliveries delivered).
rca of the issue: Root cause: ResourceInput has numeric fields with defaults (amount=0, value=0, quantity=1). Using model_dump(exclude_none=True) still emitted these default-zero values when the client sent only {status:...}, because Pydantic populated defaults != None. Fix: exclude_unset=True only serializes fields explicitly provided by the client, preserving DB values for untouched fields.
